{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVrXwhM8AAAABegTkAA", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4BrPg-zhIBbXw", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4BrPg-", "number": 1, "title": "Add contributor templates, development and review policies, UI/UX and test/CI principles, and AGENTS.md", "body": "## Problem

three-nn has an empty initial commit and needs shared contributor and agent guidance before implementation work begins. Establish the same small documentation baseline used in recent managed repositories.

## Expected outcome

Add these eight files, adapting the referenced guidance to three-nn:

- `README.md` as a truthful documentation index
- `AGENTS.md`
- `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/issue.md`
- `.github/pull_request_template.md`
- `docs/development-flow.md`
- `docs/review-guidelines.md`
- `docs/ui-ux-principles.md`
- `docs/testing-ci-principles.md`

Keep policy definitions in the canonical guides and link to them from AGENTS.md and the templates.

## Context and references

The initial empty main commit is [025b777](https://github.com/takahirox/three-nn/commit/025b7773233ab8ceb250e702876849e0f8054bc5).

Use these examples for structure and general principles:

- [cognix baseline Issue #1](https://github.com/takahirox/cognix/issues/1)
- [cognix AGENTS.md](https://github.com/takahirox/cognix/blob/main/AGENTS.md), [development flow](https://github.com/takahirox/cognix/blob/main/docs/development-flow.md) and [review guidance](https://github.com/takahirox/cognix/blob/main/docs/review-guidelines.md)
- [cognix UI/UX principles](https://github.com/takahirox/cognix/blob/main/docs/ui-ux-principles.md) and [test/CI principles](https://github.com/takahirox/cognix/blob/main/docs/testing-ci-principles.md)
- [three-motionbricks development flow](https://github.com/takahirox/three-motionbricks/blob/main/docs/development-flow.md) and [test/CI principles](https://github.com/takahirox/three-motionbricks/blob/main/docs/testing-ci-principles.md)

Adapt names, links and examples. The product scope and implementation stack of three-nn are not defined by this Issue.

## Required guidance

### Templates and collaboration

Use English for repository documentation, agent guidance, templates, Issue/PR text, reviews and commit messages.

The Issue template should capture the problem, expected outcome, context, stable acceptance identifiers such as AC1, actual validation, optional checks and genuinely required post-merge verification. The PR template should describe the resulting behavior, related Issue, evidence for each criterion, actual results and remaining scope. Use closing references when the complete Issue is resolved.

### Development, review and merge

Describe Issue → implementation → PR → review → revision → merge.

- Prefer the smallest coherent change that fulfills the Issue. Assess both missing requirements and unnecessary scope, abstractions, frameworks, dependencies and configuration.
- Review the full current Issue against the actual current PR head. Fix demonstrated defects and unmet requirements through the normal revision flow.
- Preserve approved owner decisions and current scope. A later clarification should replace the superseded requirement.
- Wait for pending CI or a resolved blocker before repeating an unchanged review, publication or merge attempt. Classify failures before fixing or retrying.
- Distinguish code defects from genuinely missing external evidence or decisions. State the reason and resume condition for a real blocker.
- Ordinary implementation choices and optional manual follow-up should not become new human-approval gates. Keep optional later checks outside completion criteria.
- Preserve the repository/workflow's existing merge authorization. Merge the reviewed head after the applicable required checks pass.
- Label authorized partial work accurately and retain its unfinished requirements. Post-merge-only checks are completion requirements only when the actual Issue explicitly requires them.

### UI/UX and layout

Define general principles that apply when a user-facing interface is introduced:

- Keep it simple, show results directly, and make interactions intuitive and predictable.
- Prioritize the main task/content/result. Place controls near their effects and group related controls.
- Use spacing, alignment and hierarchy. Remove redundant headings, repeated explanations, decorative status text and unnecessary panels.
- Keep frequent actions discoverable and reveal advanced controls when relevant.
- Support responsive layouts, keyboard access, logical focus, accessible names, readable contrast and actionable feedback.
- Preserve necessary consent and destructive-action safeguards.

### Tests and CI performance

- Catch concrete defects at the lightest meaningful layer. Use expensive integration/browser/device checks for boundaries that need them.
- Match validation to the change and actual tooling. Documentation changes need documentation checks.
- Avoid implementation-mirroring tests, equivalent duplicate suites and automatic combinations of every environment/input/state.
- Prefer small representative fixtures. Justify large datasets, downloads and external services with additional defect coverage.
- Reuse appropriate builds and cached assets. Avoid duplicate validation of the same revision and cancel superseded work when safe.
- Choose parallelism from measured resource use and elapsed time. Investigate CI growth and introduce measured budgets when executable tooling exists.
- Keep commands, outcomes and skip reasons accurate. A pending or unperformed check is not a pass.

## Mandatory pre-merge acceptance

- [ ] **AC1:** Both templates have valid GitHub syntax, stable acceptance identifiers, actual validation fields and explicit scope/remaining-work handling.
- [ ] **AC2:** Development guidance defines the workflow, English collaboration convention, focused implementation and checks appropriate to actual tooling.
- [ ] **AC3:** Review/merge guidance addresses full-Issue acceptance, owner clarifications, actual blockers, pending CI, unchanged-loop prevention, existing authorization and accurate partial completion.
- [ ] **AC4:** The canonical UI/UX guide covers the principles above without prescribing an application layout or selecting a framework.
- [ ] **AC5:** The test/CI guide covers meaningful coverage, lightweight layers, change-based checks, representative fixtures, caching, duplication and measured runtime/resource costs.
- [ ] **AC6:** AGENTS.md and README link the canonical documents and templates with consistent three-nn names. Validate template metadata, Markdown structure, local links/anchors, cross-document consistency and whitespace across the complete PR diff, including added files. Record the actual checks and results.

## Scope

This Issue adds documentation and templates. Avoid product implementation, framework/package scaffolding, new dependencies and executable test/CI/deployment workflows solely for this baseline. Use available lightweight checks for the documents.

## Validation already performed

**Pass (repository inspection):** Verified the empty initial main commit and reviewed the recent cognix baseline and template structure.

**Not run:** Checks for the files to be authored. Run and report the applicable lightweight checks on the PR.

## Optional validation

None required.

## Required post-merge verification

None required.
